is_anopheles.evidence: The study uses Anopheles gambiae s.l. (KISUMU, AKRON, and VKPER strains) for bioassays and experimental hut trials.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper does not report any genotyping of insecticide-resistance markers (e.g., kdr, Ace-1, etc.). It only mentions that the AKRON and VKPER strains are resistant to pyrethroids and that this resistance is mediated by target-site mutations (L1014F kdr and Ace-1R) based on previous studies (page 6, 8).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotype data (counts or frequencies) are reported for any mosquito populations.

african_field_population.evidence: The study involves field-aged nets collected from households in Mozambique and experimental hut trials conducted in Benin using wild mosquito populations.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study evaluating the durability of ITNs.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study specifies collection sites in Changara, Gurue, Guro, and Mandimba districts of Mozambique (page 3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study covers a collection period from 2020 to 2022 (page 3).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study is part of the New Nets Project, but it reports original data on net durability from specific districts in Mozambique.

supplement.evidence: The paper provides all necessary information regarding the bioassay results and chemical analysis in the main text and tables.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the durability of various next-generation ITNs (Olyset Plus, Royal Guard, Interceptor G2) and standard pyrethroid-only nets distributed in Mozambique (2020-2022). Bioefficacy was assessed via laboratory cone/tunnel tests and experimental hut trials in Benin. No insecticide-resistance marker genotyping was performed.
